title: FP8 signal stabilizer: layer-gated activation, hysteresis, and calibration playbook for Hopper E4M3/E5M2
creator: Evelyn Park
description: Problem: Enabling FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) on Hopper for production traffic has produced transient accuracy regressions tied to per-layer signal variance and bursty activation patterns. Current global-profile activation causes noisy layer-level tails to flip quant modes, producing non-deterministic regressions across batches. Goal: Implement a 'signal stabilizer' that (1) performs per-layer gating with short-term hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping during bursts, (2) integrates a canary sampling pipeline that exercises representative production prompts for golden-seed regression checks, and (3) wires calibration snapshots + automatic fallback to INT8/FP16 variants when stability thresholds are breached. This ticket scopes implementation, validation, observability, and a rollout plan for safe FP8 activation on Hopper with clear rollback paths.
acceptance_criteria: Per-layer gating implemented in runtime with configurable hysteresis window and thresholds (config knobs exposed in model profile)
Canary sampler service emits daily mini-batches (1k examples) covering common prompt length distribution and known edge clusters
Calibration snapshots saved per-deployment and used for rapid rollback; rollback latency < 2m from trigger
Telemetry dashboards show layer-level activation rates and hysteresis state; alerts fire when deviation > 2x baseline for >5m
End-to-end golden-seed evals show no >0.6% downstream metric regression vs baseline for 95% of sampled workloads
Automated safety fallback triggers to INT8 variant or FP16 fallback without request loss; SLO for 99th p99 latency preserved within 1.2x baseline under fallback
notes: Preliminary perf microbench: PR #1298 in github.com/redwood-inference/runtime (WIP)
